tool_input.content:
{
  "primary_frame": "Identify which employee features, if any, are meaningful predictors of performance_rating",
  "alternative_frames": [
    "Predict salary_band from employee characteristics and performance",
    "Segment employees into clusters based on work-style features (remote_pct, commute_minutes, training_hours)",
    "Assess whether satisfaction_score is driven by workplace factors or is independent"
  ],
  "required_checks": [
    "Compute pairwise correlations among all numeric features and test significance with Bonferroni correction",
    "Run a permutation-based feature importance test against performance_rating to guard against spurious fits",
    "Check whether a baseline model (mean predictor) is statistically indistinguishable from any fitted model",
    "Verify that salary_band levels show meaningful separation on numeric features via ANOVA or Kruskal-Wallis",
    "Inspect commute_minutes for right-skew outliers before modeling"
  ],
  "framing_risks": [
    "No target variable is explicitly labeled; performance_rating is assumed but may not be the intended outcome",
    "Feature distributions appear diffuse with no visible structure in the sample, raising the risk that no genuine signal exists",
    "With 9 candidate predictors and 800 rows, multiple-testing inflation could surface spurious correlations",
    "salary_band frequency is uneven (L5: 170 vs others); class imbalance may distort any classification frame",
    "Absence of domain metadata makes it impossible to distinguish meaningful from coincidental associations"
  ]
}
